newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria detains Briton for alleged fraud.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria detains Briton for alleged fraud.

text.p: A British national is being detained in Nigeria over alleged advance fee fraud known here as "419" after a section of the criminal code dealing with fraud, the semi-official Daily Times newspaper reported on Saturday.

It said William Beecham was arrested by a special police squad for allegedly attempting to collect $4.9 million as part of mobilisation fee for a fake $65 million contract between his company and state oil firm Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC).
A British high commission (embassy) spokesman said he was reading of the case for the first time and checking on it.
Beecham, a burly man of about 50, was paraded with his alleged Nigerian accomplice before Nigerian journalists in Lagos on Friday and later shown on national television.

The police commissioner in charge of the special fraud unit, who gave her name as Mrs Waziri, said Beecham was arrested at Lagos airport on June 9 and displayed NNPC and central bank documents found on him which she said were fake.
She said the arrest was the result of intensified efforts to stamp out the menace of advance fee fraud.
Nigeria has a reputation abroad of local fraudsters enticing foreigners with tempting contracts that turn out to be fake while they collect money from their victims in advance.
A Nigerian tribunal in January sentenced a British national, John Nolan, along with three Nigerians to 10 years in prison in Nigeria for smuggling marijuana.
